_README: Published inputs for the table recovery, one entry per comparison in Table 3 of paper/criterion_agreement_v5.tex. Every value is transcribed from the artifact named in source_artifact and pinned by sha256 in reference/FETCH_LOG.json; quote records the sentence it was read from. Numeric figures are strings carrying the source's own printed digits, because 0.10 and 0.100 are the same float and imply different rounding intervals. marginals_as_percent says whether p_A and p_B are printed as percentages. Entries with status not_attempted declare why. denominator_status is explicit_same, explicit_different, inferred or unclear; only explicit_same supports a strong reconstruction. kappa_variant must be unweighted Cohen, since weighted, Fleiss, PABAK and AC1 kappas do not satisfy the identity. unit_of_analysis records what N counts, because visits and lesions are not patients. criterion_A fixes which marginal is which, and positive_category which class counts as positive, because directional discordance is not symmetric under either swap.

guerra2026.criteria: Neurologist-assigned SPMS label (A) against trial protocol definition (B)
guerra2026.quote: Among them, 866 (4.26%) were classified as SPMS according to ND and 1603 (7.89%) according to the HERCULES definition. Table 3, headed "Neurologist's definition as Gold Standard", reports true positive 326, false negative 540, false positive 1277, true negative 18,163 on N = 20,306.
guerra2026.note: The source publishes the joint table and no agreement statistic: it reports sensitivity, specificity, predictive values, accuracy and a C-index against the neurologist's definition, nominated as the reference. The kappa entered here was computed by this analysis from those cells, so this row's self-test is circular and establishes only that the round trip returns a superset. The row is retained because the plan forbids removing a row after results are seen; it is reported with the circularity named.
guerra2026.denominator_note: Table 3 gives the four cells and the percentages of the same N = 20,306.
guerra2026.reported_as: accuracy against a nominated reference standard

westbury2023.quote: The proportion of participants with sarcopenia in the whole sample according to each definition was as follows: EWGSOP2 (1.1%), SDOC (1.7%) ... kappa = 0.17 when cohorts were pooled. Table 2, under the column headed All cohorts (n = 9170), gives EWGSOP2 105 (1.1%) and SDOC 152 (1.7%).
westbury2023.denominator_note: n = 9170 is itself the complete-case sample, restricted to men with complete data on every analysis variable; both prevalences and the kappa are stated on it. The residual ambiguity is whether "pooled" means the kappa was computed on the 9170 or meta-analytically across the five cohort kappas, which are not shown.

daghi2026.criteria: 5-2-1 criteria (A) against neurologist judgment (B), advanced disease
daghi2026.quote: The 5-2-1 criteria classified 44.6% of patients as having APD, while neurologists identified 43.2%. The two assessments aligned in 73% of cases, indicating moderate agreement (kappa = 0.48). A total of 370 patients.
daghi2026.note: Over-determined: N, both marginals, kappa AND raw agreement are published, so the recovery has an independent check.
daghi2026.denominator_note: Both proportions, the 73% alignment and kappa are all reported on the 370 included patients.

meagher2014_strict.cells_provenance: printed in the Results text, disaggregated rather than tabulated
meagher2014_strict.quote: Only 155 cases were identified as delirium by all three approaches and 455 were identified by both DSM-IV and relaxed DSM-5. There were three cases of delirium unique to the strict DSM-5 versus DSM-IV group, compared to 355 DSM-IV cases of delirium negative by the strict interpretation of DSM-5. There were 55 delirium cases unique to DSM-IV as compared to either DSM-5 group ... Further, 11 patients met DSM-5 relaxed criteria but not DSM-IV delirium. The concordance between the different diagnostic methods for the whole dataset was 53% (k = 0.22) between DSM-IV and the strict DSM-5, 91% (k = 0.82) between the DSM-IV and relaxed DSM-5 criteria and 60% (k = 0.29) between the strict versus relaxed DSM-5 criteria. Using DSM-IV by clinical assessment, delirium was found in 510/768 patients (66%). Strict DSM-5 criteria categorized 158 as delirious ... whereas relaxed DSM-5 criteria identified 466 as delirious.
meagher2014_strict.note: Self-test. The source prints all four cells in prose and both summary statistics, so the recovery must contain the published table.
meagher2014_strict.denominator_note: All three comparisons are reported on the one pooled cohort of 768 patients; the cell counts printed in the Results sum to 768 for each pair.

meagher2014_reading.quote: The concordance between the different diagnostic methods for the whole dataset was 53% (k = 0.22) between DSM-IV and the strict DSM-5, 91% (k = 0.82) between the DSM-IV and relaxed DSM-5 criteria and 60% (k = 0.29) between the strict versus relaxed DSM-5 criteria. meagher2014_reading.note: Recovery target. The source prints both marginals and both summary statistics for this pair but not its cells. The two readings differ only in how permissively one criterion set is applied, so the strict class is contained in the relaxed class by construction; whether the published figures force that containment is what the enumeration decides.
meagher2014_reading.denominator_note: All three comparisons are reported on the one pooled cohort of 768 patients; the cell counts printed in the Results sum to 768 for each pair.

mana2026_differing.criteria: Algorithms differing only in the functional-impairment rule
mana2026_differing.reason: Reports kappa as a mean over many algorithm pairs with an SD, not a single pairwise table. The full pairwise matrix is shipped as data in an R package (github.com/josefmana/demcrit); recovering from it is a different procedure than the identity registered here.

inoue2012_fpg.criteria: JDS (A) against ADA fasting plasma glucose (B)
inoue2012_fpg.cells_provenance: Table 2, printed as counts with row percentages
inoue2012_fpg.quote: Using the first and second checkups, 174 (2.4%) and 175 (2.4%) were diagnosed as FPG diabetes and HbA1c diabetes according to the ADA criteria, respectively. Among 153 subjects diagnosed with diabetes by the JDS criteria, 125 (81.7%) and 129 (84.3%) fulfilled the ADA-FPG and ADA-HbA1c criteria of diabetes, respectively. ... finally 7,328 persons were enrolled for this study. The kappa coefficients between the JDS criteria and ADA-FPG or ADA-HbA1c criteria were 0.759 (P<0.001) and 0.782 (P<0.001), respectively. On the other hand, the kappa coefficient between the ADA-FPG and ADA-HbA1c criteria was 0.668 (P<0.001).
inoue2012_fpg.denominator_note: Table 2 reports both comparisons on the enrolled 7,328, and its cells sum to 7,328 in each panel.
